summary: MTT-semantics after Chatzikyriakidis & Luo 2020: CNs as types with polymorphic quantifiers; coercive subtyping rendered by explicit liftings with the every/some/no monotonicity package; judgmental interpretations and propositional forms; the full §3.3 adjective case study (intersective iff via Sigma, subsective non-transferability proved by countermodel, privative sum types with the gun partition, non-committal opacity witness); veridical adverbs as Sigma-packaged modifiers; copredication through a two-projection dot-type record; individuation with phy- vs info-counting on a concrete two-copy lexicon; an NLI mini-suite. Zero axioms and zero Parameters, unlike the ttr_mtt/ pilots and CL20's own Appendix 7 code.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. ISTE/Wiley.
Luo, Z. (2012). Common nouns as types. LACL.
Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2014). Natural language inference in Coq. JoLLI.

evidence: The adjective case study follows §3.3 class by class, with the negative data (subsective non-transfer, non-committal opacity) PROVED as countermodel existence theorems rather than asserted.
Dot-type elimination behaviour matches App. 6 for the copredication sentences used.
All 14 audited theorems closed under the global context (grep count of Axiom/Parameter: zero).
simplifications: CN is the ambient Type, not an internal universe
individuation is the count-2 fragment of §5.3
subtyping coherence unchecked (Coq has no coherence checker)
additions: zero-axiom discipline replacing the Parameter/Axiom style of the ttr_mtt/ pilots and CL20 App. 7
explicit countermodels for the negative adjective data

determination_rationale: The CL20 analyses go through with no axioms once the lexicon is section-quantified; the encoding gaps (internal universe, dot-type pairing, coercion coherence) are representational and documented per artifact class.
